findings.issue: contradicts task clause P4.6-w15 ('only the orchestrator writes architecture.model.json'): Hard rule 1 still reads 'The agents write only the model', which says the agents write the model. The synthesizer and reviewer have no write tools (agents/archmap-synthesizer.md, agents/archmap-reviewer.md) and the explorer writes nothing. SKILL.md now states two opposite things, and the Hard rules are the part an orchestrator reads first.
findings.resolution: Reword rule 1 to 'Only the orchestrator writes the model. Agents have no write tools for it and return JSON; scripts write HTML, layout and issues files.' Keep the D1 point (the model is the single source of truth).

findings.issue: s5 only inspects lines that name 'synthesizer' or 'reviewer' and carry no never/not/no/without word. The stale claim at SKILL.md:17 says 'agents', so s5 passes while the contradiction in finding 1 remains. The negation filter would also let a line such as 'the synthesizer writes the model, no review needed' through.
findings.resolution: Extend the claim scan to lines that say 'agents' (or 'agent') together with a write verb and architecture.model.json or 'the model', and drop the blanket negation exclusion in favour of matching the specific allowed phrasing.

findings.issue: The 'project's own Python' recipe is `python3 -c "import duckdb; ..."` run from the analysed repo root. `python -c` puts the current directory first on sys.path, so a repo-owned duckdb.py or sqlite3.py would be imported and executed. That breaks the same file's rule (line 12) and SKILL.md hard rule 3, 'never execute the scanned project's own code'. The example also hard-codes /tmp/copy.duckdb rather than the mktemp copy from the DuckDB section.
findings.resolution: Run the recipe isolated (`python3 -I -c ...`, or `cd` to the temp dir first) and say so in the text. Point the example at the `$tmp` copy so the original is never opened.
